title.narrative: Global WASH Program(GWP) Phase II, Pakistan

description.narrative: In Pakistan, the Global WASH Programme (GWP) Phase II advances structural change through three interlinked outcomes: Integrated Inclusive Planning, Institutional Arrangements & Coordination, and Learning and Sector Adaptation. The programme supports evidence-based policy development and promotes systems approaches across all levels of government.

Micro Level (Community and Service Providers) Direct Participants: The programme directly reaches approximately 20,000 individuals at community level, including men, women, children, and people with special needs, primarily through WASH awareness-raising campaigns. Micro Level (Community and Service Providers) Indirect Participants: The wider population of around 5 million people in District Muzaffargarh and an additional district (in Punjab, Sindh, or KP) indirectly benefits from improved WASH planning, coordination, and service delivery facilitated by strengthened systems at local level. Meso Level (District Level) Direct Participants: District administrations in Muzaffargarh and at least one additional district benefit from enhanced institutional capacity for coordination, planning, and implementation of WASH services. Additionally, approximately 1,110 individuals from government institutions and other stakeholders gain directly from capacity-building activities, advocacy events, and coordination platforms. Meso Level (District Level) Indirect Participants: Government departments and civil society organizations within these districts benefit indirectly through improved frameworks for collaboration and execution of WASH interventions. Macro Level (Provincial and National Level) Direct Participants: At the macro level, Punjab province is directly supported through the development of a long-term WASH Sector Development Plan and the establishment of a knowledge and resource hub. Furthermore, approximately 775 individuals from government bodies and other institutions are capacitated through training, workshops, and advocacy initiatives. Non-governmental actors such as NGOs, INGOs, and development partners also benefit from participation in knowledge-sharing processes. Macro Level (Provincial and National Level) Indirect Participants: Development organizations, INGOs, and NGOs benefit indirectly by operating within a more coherent, better-resourced enabling environment shaped by the programme’s systems-strengthening efforts.

This project is part of Phase II of the Global WASH Program (GWP) implemented in Sierra Leone, Zimbabwe , Pakistan and India. Building on Phase I, Phase II of the program focuses on scaling and institutionalizing WASH systems strengthening across five key areas: Service Delivery Strengthening, Inclusive Planning, Accountability & Monitoring, Institutional Arrangements & Coordination, and Learning & Sector Adaptation. A key emphasis is the shift from systems strengthening to systems delivery, ensuring sustainable WASH services for target communities. Phase II embeds these approaches in government structures and policies, reducing dependency on external support. Advocacy and stakeholder collaboration remain vital for financial sustainability and institutional adaptation.
